# Maṭṭhakuṇḍalījātaka (Ja 449)

**ID:** Ja 449
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Maṭṭhakuṇḍalījātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul9.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalījātaka* (Ja 449) is a narrative belonging to the Pali Jātaka collection. According to the traditional framing preserved in the text, the Buddha delivered this discourse while residing at Jetavana near Sāvatthī, prompted by a landowner who was so overwhelmed by grief after the death of his beloved son that he neglected bathing, eating, work, and attendance on the Buddha.

Eugene W. Burlingame observed that the author of the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* reworked the material of Jātaka 449—merging both its introduction and its story of the past into a single unified narrative while expanding it considerably [Burlingame 1921]. He further noted that the conversion of Maṭṭhakuṇḍalī by the Buddha, which forms a central element in the *Dhammapada* commentary and its derivative version in the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, is absent from the Jātaka version itself [Burlingame 1921].
